primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: After prolonged starvation, carbohydrate refeeding causes an insulin surge that drives phosphate, potassium, and magnesium into cells while total-body stores are depleted. The resulting hypophosphatemia can impair ATP generation, cardiac conduction, and respiratory-muscle function.
vignette: A severely malnourished patient begins high-carbohydrate enteral feeding after a prolonged period of minimal intake. Two days later, the patient develops generalized weakness, confusion, peripheral edema, and a new ventricular arrhythmia. Serum phosphate is markedly decreased.
lead: Which of the following physiologic changes most directly explains the new hypophosphatemia?
correct: An insulin-mediated shift of phosphate into cells superimposed on depleted total-body phosphate stores
distractors: Respiratory alkalosis causing acute intracellular phosphate redistribution despite normal total-body stores
FGF23 excess causing renal internalization of sodium-phosphate cotransporters
Parathyroid hormone excess causing isolated renal phosphate wasting
Massive cell lysis causing release of intracellular phosphate into the circulation
distractor_notes: Respiratory alkalosis can shift phosphate intracellularly, but the defining refeeding mechanism is insulin-driven uptake in a patient with depleted total-body stores after starvation.
FGF23-mediated phosphaturia causes disorders such as tumor-induced osteomalacia or XLH, not the acute post-refeeding electrolyte shift.
PTH can cause renal phosphate wasting, but it does not explain the temporal relationship to carbohydrate refeeding after prolonged starvation.
Cell lysis raises, rather than lowers, serum phosphate and is characteristic of tumor lysis or rhabdomyolysis.
key_expl: Starvation depletes intracellular phosphate stores even when serum concentrations may initially appear acceptable. Carbohydrate refeeding increases insulin, which drives phosphate into cells for phosphorylated intermediates and ATP production. The combination of depleted total-body stores and rapid intracellular uptake produces the hallmark hypophosphatemia of refeeding syndrome.
objective: Explain refeeding hypophosphatemia as insulin-driven intracellular phosphate uptake occurring on a background of depleted total-body phosphate.
